summary: A low, tiered rectangular two-floor building with stepped stone-slab roof layers, brick mid-walls, wooden trim, glass windows in continuous rows, and a stone-brick tower at one corner. The plan is mostly a hollow rectangle (courtyard/open central channel visible from top) with symmetric stepped roof slabs over two parallel blocks connected by a central corridor/bridge.

shape.overall_form: two parallel rectangular volumes with a central open channel and a corner vertical tower; stepped roof slabs stacked above each volume
shape.symmetry: bilaterally symmetric along the central corridor axis (front-back symmetry; left-right mirrored volumes)

elements: continuous horizontal windows spanning each face at two levels
stone-slab stepped roof in multiple tiers (overhanging slabs)
brick walls with wooden horizontal banding
stonebrick corner tower rising above main roof
glowstone or light blocks placed at facade corners (lighting accents)
central open channel/courtyard visible from top; small bridge/entrance on front
rebuild_hints: Create a rectangular base of stonebrick foundation 1-2 blocks high around footprint.
Build two stacked brick wall bands with a one-block wooden plank band between them; place continuous glass panes in a row above the wooden band on both long sides.
Add a row of stone slabs as a narrow roof cap above the glass band, then stack multiple overhanging stone slab tiers centered over each rectangular half to form stepped roofs.
Place a vertical stonebrick tower at the rear-left corner rising ~6 blocks above the roof for the chimney/tower element.
Leave a central open channel/courtyard between the two halves and add a small bridge/entry walkway across the front into that channel.
